title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reading.body:
This is a compliance failure at the power layer of a data center deployment, not a failure of a model or a software system. The site was running 62 natural gas generators that had no permits to be installed or operated, and the state treated that as a violation of the Air Pollution Control Act. The equipment was already in service, with part of the complex in use, so the gap was between physical operation and the authorisation required for it.

Catching it would have taken a permit check before the generators were energised, and a reconciliation of installed equipment against what had been approved. The state found the generators during an inspection in late July, which means the condition persisted until an outside party looked. Nothing in the reporting describes an internal control that flagged the missing permits first.

What is not established is intent, and the federal lawsuit by nearby homeowners over noise is an allegation, not a finding. The health department violation orders and the fine are enforcement actions, not court rulings, and the reporting does not say whether the generators were tied to any particular workload.

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million after state inspectors found 62 natural gas generators at its Vineland data center site in late July. The 2,000 kilowatt generators lacked required permits to be installed or operated, and the state said the fine was for violating the Air Pollution Control Act. Officials called it the largest fine ever issued to a data center operator in New Jersey.

The planned data center is a 2.6 million square foot complex that will need 350 megawatts of power, enough for a medium size city, and is slated for completion at the end of the year. Some of it is already in use. Nearby homeowners have filed a federal lawsuit over noise, and the Cumberland County Health Department has issued violation orders to DataOne for excessive noise.
